First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{z}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{z}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y+z)) \\  & =xy\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y+z)) \\  & =\frac{xy}{x+y+z}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{zy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{z}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{z}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{xy}{x+y+z}) \\  & =\frac{x\cdot (x+y+z)-xy\cdot (1)}{(x+y+z)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+xy+xz-xy}{(x+y+z)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+xz}{(x+y+z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{zyx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{zy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zyx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{zy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{x}^{2}+xz}{(x+y+z)^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(2x+z)\cdot (x+y+z)^{2}-({x}^{2}+xz)\cdot (2(x+y+z)\cdot 1)}{(x+y+z)^{4}} \\  & =\frac{(2x+z)(x+y+z)-2({x}^{2}+xz)}{(x+y+z)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{zyx}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,1,-1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{zyx}(1,1,-1) & =\frac{(2(1)+(-1))(1+1+(-1))-2({1}^{2}+1(-1))}{(1+1+(-1))^{3}}=\frac{(1)(1)-2(0)}{(1)^{3}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =2y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})) \\  & =2y\cdot \frac{2x}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4y}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{yxx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yxx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{yx}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4y}{x}) \\  & =\frac{0\cdot x-4y\cdot 1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{4y}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})) \\  & =y\cdot (-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})) \\  & =-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})-2{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y)+{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =-2y\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})-2{y}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{y}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+{y}^{2})-2y(y+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+{y}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{6} \\ {g}_{yy}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})-{g}_{yy}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}-(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\sqrt{3}.
$$

First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡xyz) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz)\cdot yz \\  & =yz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =yz\cdot (-yz\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xxz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xx}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xxz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xx}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(-{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}\cdot (2z\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)+xy{z}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz)) \\  & =-{y}^{2}z(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(xyz)+xyz\operatorname{cos}⁡(xyz))\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xxz}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,\frac{1}{2},\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xxz}(1,\frac{1}{2},\pi ) & =-{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}\cdot \pi \cdot (2\operatorname{sin}⁡(1\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi )+1\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(1\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot \pi )) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{4}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\pi }{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$
